title: Test Doubles & Contract Testing — Quick Revision

sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: Test doubles in RSpec — doubles, instance_doubles, class_doubles, and spies — are the mechanism for isolating units from their dependencies. The critical rule is to use verifying doubles (instance_double, class_double) rather than plain doubles, because verifying doubles fail if the stubbed method doesn't exist on the real class. This prevents tests from passing while production code breaks due to a method rename. WebMock stubs HTTP requests at the Net::HTTP level; VCR records and replays real HTTP interactions as cassettes. Contract testing with Pact verifies that a Rails API continues to honour the contract its consumers depend on — a safety net for microservices. This page covers all three layers with the practical gotchas that appear in senior interviews.

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: doubles-and-mocking, webmock-vcr, contract-testing. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
